s: Which one of the Chola kings conquered Ceylon?

s: Name the Chola King who conquered the northern part of Sri Lanka?

s: Who among the following carried out a naval invasion of Southeast Asia?

s: Which Chola king defeated the Sailendra king by sending a naval expedition to the Srivijaya Empire?

s:
In the context of the history of India, consider the following pairs:
Term - Description

A. Eripatti : Land, revenue from which was set apart for the maintenance of the village tank

B. Taniyurs : Villagers donated to a single Brahmin or a group of Brahmins

C. Ghatikas : Colleges generally attached to the temples

s: In the Chola Kingdom, a very large village administered as a single unit was called:
x: A taniyur was a very large village (an important brahmadeya or nagaram) run as a separate unit, independent of the nadu. Kurram and nadu were groups of villages; a kottam was a group of nadus.

s:

x: Lingaraja (Bhubaneswar) is credited to the (Eastern) Gangas in exam keys, Vaikuntha Perumal (Kanchipuram) to the Pallavas, Brihadisvara (Thanjavur) to the Cholas and Chennakeshava (Belur) to the Hoysalas. Moved.

s: The Dravidian style of architecture is found in:
x: The Dravida style (pyramidal vimana, gopurams, prakara) belongs to South India and reached its peak under the Cholas.

s: The mighty gateways found at the temples of South India are called
x: The towering gateways of South Indian (Dravida) temples are called gopurams - elaborate entrance gates, a distinctive feature of the style.

s: Which one of the following statements about Brihadeswara Temple at Tanjavur is not correct?
o: The temple is a splendid example of Chola architecture.
It was built by Emperor Rajaraja I.
The temple is constructed of granite.
The temple is a monument dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
x: The Brihadeswara temple is a Shiva temple (with one of India's largest lingas and Shiva as Tripurantaka), not a Vishnu monument. It is Chola work, built by Rajaraja I, of granite.

s: The Tamil Poet and Author of Ramayana in Tamil Kamban was in the court of which Kings?
x: Kamban wrote the Tamil Ramayana (Ramavataram) at the court of the Chola king Kulottunga III, not under the Hoysalas, Pandyas or Cheras.

s: Who among the following was the author of the Tamil Ramayanam or Ramavataram ?
x: Kamban wrote the Tamil Ramayana (Ramavataram) under Chola patronage in the 12th century. Nannaya and Tikkana wrote the Telugu Mahabharata.

s: Which one of the following pairs is incorrect about the temples and their location?
x: The Golden Temple is at Amritsar, not Amaravati, so that pair is wrong. Brihadeeswara is at Thanjavur, Chennakeshava at Belur and the Madhavaraya temple inside Gandikota fort (Kadapa).

s: Hoysala monuments are found in :
x: Hoysala monuments are at Halebid (Hoysaleswara) and Belur (Chennakeshava); Hampi is Vijayanagara.

s: Which of the following temple is an example of Vesara style of architecture?
x: The Hoysaleswara temple at Halebidu is a Hoysala temple, classed in exams as Vesara (neither fully Nagara nor Dravida). Kandariya Mahadeva is Nagara.

s:
Consider the following properties included in the World Heritage List released by UNESCO:
1. Shantiniketan
2. Rani-ki-Vav
3. Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas
4. Mahabodhi Bodhgaya Temple Complex at Bodhgaya
How many of the above properties were included in 2023?
x: Only two were inscribed in 2023: Santiniketan and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas. Rani-ki-Vav was listed in 2014 and the Mahabodhi temple in 2002.

s: “Dwarasamudra’ was the capital of which dynastic power?
x: Dwarasamudra (Halebidu) was the capital of the Hoysalas; Warangal was the Kakatiya capital and Banavasi the Kadamba capital.

s: What is modern name of Hoysaleshvara’s ancient capital of Dwarasamudra?
x: The Hoysala capital Dwarasamudra is the present Halebid (Halebidu, 'old city') in Hassan district, Karnataka.

s:
Consider the following dynasties:
1. Hoysala
2. Gahadavala
3. Kakatiya
4. Yadava
How many of the above dynasties established their kingdoms in early eighth century AD?
x: None: the Hoysalas (independent late 12th c.), Gahadavalas (c. 1089), Kakatiyas (12th c.) and Yadavas (12th c.) all rose after the 8th century.

s: The King who was defeated by Malik Kafur was
x: Malik Kafur defeated the Yadava king Ramachandra of Devagiri in 1307 and took him to Delhi. (He also forced the Hoysala Vira Ballala III to submit in 1310-11, so 'Vira Ballala' is also defensible; Rudramadevi died in 1289.)

s: What was the mother tongue of the Devagiri Yadavas?
x: The Seuna Yadavas of Devagiri ruled Maharashtra and their mother tongue was Marathi, which they encouraged; Sanskrit was only the language of scholarship. Telugu was the Kakatiyas' language, Kannada the Hoysalas'.

s: Mother tongue of the Devagiri Yadavas?
x: The Devagiri (Seuna) Yadavas ruled present-day Maharashtra and their mother tongue was Marathi; they patronised Marathi literature (Dnyaneshwari, Lilacharitra). Telugu, Kannada and Urdu do not fit.

s: Among the following who established Devagiri as an independent Yadava Kingdom?
x: Bhillama V threw off Kalyani Chalukya rule, declared independence and built Devagiri (c. 1187) as the Yadava capital. Prola I, Prola II and Ganapati were Kakatiya rulers.

s: Which Yadava king defeated Rudradeva?
x: Yadava Jaitugi (Jaitrapala) defeated and killed Kakatiya Rudradeva and held the young Ganapatideva captive (Hemadri; Paithan plate). Rudradeva is the victim, not the victor.

s: Rudramadevi's victory over the Devagiri Yadavas is recorded in which of the following inscriptions?
x: The Bidar fort inscription records Rudramadevi's victory over the Yadava king Mahadeva. Chandupatla records her death, Bayyaram is Mailamba's tank record and Hanumakonda is Rudradeva's 1163 record.

s: The Famous king in Yadavaraja Dynasty?
x: Singhana (Simhana II) was the greatest Yadava king of Devagiri; Ramachandra lost to Alauddin, Bhima II was a Chaulukya and Virarajendra a Chola.

s: Who was the famous Sanskrit scholar of the Devagiri Yadava period and author of Chaturvarga Chintamani?
x: Hemadri, minister (Shrikaranadhipa) of the Yadavas Mahadeva and Ramachandra, wrote the Sanskrit encyclopaedia Chaturvarga Chintamani. Vidyanatha and Jayapa served the Kakatiyas, Palkuriki Somanatha was a Telugu Saiva poet.

s: 'Lilavati' a treatise on Mathematics, was written by –
x: Lilavati, the arithmetic part of the Siddhanta Shiromani, was written by Bhaskaracharya (Bhaskara II, 12th c.), whose grandson Changadeva taught his works at Patan under the Yadavas. Ramanuja, Kautilya and Amartya Sen wrote no such work.

s: Famous Sanskrit scholar of the time of the Devagiri Yadavas and author of Chaturvarga Chintamani?
x: Hemadri, the Yadava minister, wrote Chaturvarga Chintamani on dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas. Vidyanatha (Kakatiya court poet), Jayapa Senani (Nrittaratnavali) and Palkuriki Somanatha are wrong.

s: Who was the ruler of Devgiri at the time of Alauddin Khalji’s invasion?
x: Ramachandra (Ramadeva) ruled Devagiri when Alauddin Khalji raided it in 1296 and again faced Malik Kafur in 1307. Prataparudra was the Kakatiya king, Malik Kafur a Khalji general and Ratan Singh the Rana of Chittor.
